title: Key Account Admission Criteria and FastPass Lane for Critical Escalations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a lightweight, auditable "FastPass" intake lane for top accounts that accelerates evaluation, commitment decisions, and delivery windows for critical escalations. This ticket defines admission criteria, decision gates, SLA for response/commit, documentation templates, and an operational playbook for cross-functional execution.

Problem statement:
Top enterprise customers are currently routed through the standard intake funnel which averages 6-8 weeks from ask to roadmap commitment. For strategic accounts facing production-impacting issues or time-sensitive feature requests tied to renewals, this latency causes churn risk and executive escalations. We need a repeatable, low-friction path that preserves fairness and auditability while enabling faster internal prioritization and delivery.

Goals:
- Create a clear, defensible admission rubric for the FastPass lane (criteria + evidence).
- Establish SLA targets for initial evaluation (48 business hours) and commitment decision (7 business days).
- Define the commit types supported (investigator, delivery timeline, funded work) and fallback policies.
- Produce templates (GDoc + intake form) and a Slack triage flowbook.
- Implement lightweight tracking in the roadmap board and console (tags + tiered notifications).
- Pilot with 3 strategic accounts in Q2 and measure time-to-decision and renewal impact.

Proposed solution:
1) Admission rubric: must include account tier (Enterprise Tier A), measurable impact (SLO/regression/customer revenue at risk), and executive sponsor sign-off. Evidence required: production incident report or contract clause + expected business outcome.
2) Triage flow: incoming escalation -> PM intake -> 48h business evaluation by triage pod (PM, Solutions Eng, CSM, Eng lead) -> decision: (a) Immediate ops/mitigation (b) FastPass commit (timeboxed roadmap slot) (c) Decline with alternatives.
3) Commit types:
   - Hotfix/mitigation (operational)
   - Short-scope feature (<= 2 sprints)
   - Funded feature with separate contract (T&Cs)
4) Transparency: every FastPass case gets a dedicated notes doc, tracking tags in the roadmap, and a one-line update in fortnightly account health digest.

Acceptance criteria:
- Admission rubric doc published and signed by Head of Customer Success and Eng Manager.
- Intake form + GDoc template created and linked from the PM playbook.
- Triage runbook with role RACI and SLA timers added to Confluence.
- Roadmap board has FastPass tag and two custom fields (Admission Date, Decision Date).
- Pilot kickoff scheduled with Sales and three named accounts.

Success metrics:
- Median initial evaluation time <= 48 business hours for pilot cases.
- Median decision time <= 7 business days.
- Pilot NPS delta for participating accounts +5 vs baseline.
- Two pilot cases convert to paid funded scope or removal of renewal risk.

Stakeholders:

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07): Draft rubric + templates.
- Week 2 (2026-03-08 to 2026-03-14): Review with CS, Sales, Eng; incorporate feedback.
- Week 3 (2026-03-15 to 2026-03-21): Publish docs, implement roadmap tags, train triage pod.
- Week 4 (2026-03-22 to 2026-03-28): Pilot launches with first two accounts.
- Week 7 (2026-04-12): Pilot review and retrospective; decide go/no-go for broader roll.

Rollout plan:
- Pilot (Q2): 3 accounts, weekly cadence updates, tight feedback loop.
- Iterate rubric and SLAs after pilot.
- Q3: Expand to top 20 strategic accounts and add dashboard tile in Console for FastPass queues.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should funded features require a separate project/track or be treated as prioritized roadmap work? (Legal & Finance input required)
- How to prevent abuse / overuse: consider quota per account per year or executive sponsor confirmation.
- Do we allow overlapping FastPass commits to displace existing queued roadmap work? Define guardrails to avoid rework.

Progress log (chronological):
- 2026-03-01 (Ava Chen): Created ticket and initial rubric draft. Shared with CS.
- 2026-03-03 (Diego Marquez): Reviewed draft; recommended narrowing commitment types to avoid open-ended promises.
- 2026-03-05 (Priya Rao): CS feedback: require CS owner confirmation + customer impact evidence checklist.
- 2026-03-08 (Ava Chen): Incorporated CS feedback. Shared PRD v0.2: link above.
- 2026-03-09 (Marco Hernandez): Sales sponsor: proposed pilot accounts and suggested including renewal timeline as a field on intake form.
- 2026-03-10 (Diego Marquez): Raised engineering constraints: short-scope feature definition must map to <= 1 FTE-week of work or be classified as funded. Added to rubric.
- 2026-03-12 (Ava Chen): Finalized SLA timers and published triage runbook draft. Seeking Legal & Finance review for funded work template (assigned).

Review feedback captured:
- Eng (Diego): prefer automated tagging and alerts from intake form to cut manual overhead. Action: ENG-automation spike scoped (ENG-1842).
- CS (Priya): add post-decision communication templates and standard account-health update cadence. Action: create templates (owner: Priya).
- Sales (Marco): tighten acceptance criteria for measurable ROI to avoid subjective prioritization.

Next steps (owner):
- Legal & Finance to review funded-work T&Cs by 2026-03-19 (owner: Legal team).
- ENG to ship intake -> roadmap automation spike (ENG-1842) to validate tags and timers (owner: Diego).
- CSM to prepare communication templates and update pilot account playbooks (owner: Priya).
- PM to schedule pilot kickoff with three accounts and Sales sponsors (owner: Ava).

Notes & follow-ups:
- If pilot shows consistent >7 day decision times, escalate to Executive Ops for temporary capacity reallocation.
- Consider adding a small funded "FastPass buffer" budget for high-priority urgent work if pilot workload is recurring.
